Buildings Department    Registered Structural Engineers and          APP-32
                        Registered Geotechnical Engineers


      Hong Kong Airport (Control of Obstructions) Ordinance (Cap. 301)


Airport Height Restrictions

            The Hong Kong Airport (Control of Obstructions) Ordinance (Cap. 301)
provides for, among others, the restriction of heights of buildings in the interest of
ensuring aviation safety.  The airport height restrictions (AHRs) vary at different
locations of Hong Kong and these height limits are set out in a series of Airport Height
Restriction Plans which are deposited in the Land Registry and can be purchased from
the Map Publications Centres of the Lands Department. For details, please refer to the
website of Civil Aviation Department at www.cad.gov.hk.

Exemption from AHRs

2.           Temporary  exemption  from  AHRs  may  be  applied  from  the
Director-General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). Subject to such terms and conditions, this
kind of temporary exemption will normally be valid for a period not exceeding two
months, which may be extended for further periods of two months as DGCA thinks fit.

3.                If any projects are being or to be carried out in an area which is subject to
AHRs, authorized persons and registered structural engineers are requested to ensure
that the responsible registered contractor obtains the prior approval of DGCA to any
item of temporary plant or equipment likely to project beyond the prescribed height
limits  at any time during construction.   Guidelines for registered contractors are
provided in the Practice Note for Registered Contractors 7.

Third Runway of the Hong Kong International Airport

4.         To cater for the changes in airspace protection requirements necessitated
by the third runway and the three-runway system at the Hong Kong International Airport
(HKIA),  the Hong Kong  Airport  (Control  of  Obstructions)  (No.2) Order 1997
(Amendment) Order 2021 which prescribes the new AHRs will come into operation on
31 May 2022. Under the new AHRs, certain areas in the vicinity of HKIA, mainly the
surrounding sea or mountainous areas, will be subject to more stringent restrictions,





                                                                            /while …

while the remaining areas constituting the majority of Hong Kong will be subject to less
stringent AHRs. The new AHRs will not apply to any building erected in accordance
with plans approved by the Building Authority before 31 May 2022 and any minor
works and designated exempted works completed before 31 May 2022.





                                                          ( YU Po-mei, Clarice )
                                              Building Authority
